name: ESP32-C3 SuperMini
blurb: Thumb-sized Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE controller with USB-C, 16 pins and an onboard blue LED.

pins.note: ADC2 channel: analogue reads are unreliable while Wi-Fi is on. Also an SPI pin.
Drives the onboard blue LED, which lights when the pin is LOW (inverted). Strapping pin: do not hold it low at reset. Default I2C SDA in the Arduino core.
Wired to the BOOT button and sampled at reset: holding it low at power-up enters download mode instead of running your program. Default I2C SCL.
UART0 RX. USB serial uses the native USB port, so this pin is free for a second serial device.
UART0 TX. USB serial uses the native USB port, so this pin is free for a second serial device.

pins.name: 5V
pins.note: 5 V straight from the USB-C port when plugged in. Also the pin to feed 5 V into when running without USB. Never power from both at once through a separate supply.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.note: Output of the onboard 3.3 V regulator. The chip itself takes most of its capacity during Wi-Fi bursts, so keep external loads small.

search: ESP32-C3 Super Mini development board USB-C

verify: Clone board with no official drawing or open board file found; batches differ. Confirmed by independent sources: outline 22.5 (22.52) x 18 mm, 0.1 in pitch, 15.24 mm between rows. NOT confirmed by any source: PCB thickness (modelled 1.0; measure it, clones are often 0.8 to 1.2), distance from the USB-C front edge to the first pad (modelled 3.24), USB-C shell width and overhang (modelled flush, 8.94 wide), all shape heights, LED and button positions. Variants: the 'Plus' and v2 boards have different outlines and pin counts; this file is the plain 16-pin board. Some listings and ESPHome pages use SDA=GPIO5/SCL=GPIO6 as software defaults; the Arduino default is GPIO8/GPIO9. Supply: sources quote the 5V pin as 3.3-6 V or 5-7 V and 3V3 output as 150 to 500 mA; the modelled 150 mA is the conservative figure. With calipers measure: PCB length and width; PCB thickness; distance from the USB-C front edge to the first pad; USB-C width and overhang. Confirm LED polarity (modelled active-low on GPIO8) and which row carries 5V/GND/3V3 with USB at the top and the component side up. Both buttons (BOOT, RST) are not modelled because their position is unverified; measure them if the case needs access. Pin y-positions come from the Wokwi board definition, which is drawn on an 18 x 24.576 mm canvas (artwork derived from the Adafruit QT Py ESP32-C3, per its own description) while the real board is 22.5 mm long, so the offset from the USB edge is an assumption: measure it. Component positions on the board face (chip, antenna, buttons) are drawn for recognition only; rely on the outline and pad positions.
sources: https://protosupplies.com/product/esp32c3-supermini/ (seller: 22.5 x 18 mm, 15.24 mm row spacing, 0.1 in pitch, 130 mA typical)
